primary_theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery
action_summary: Combat trafficking in persons
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Accelerate the process of effective implementation of the national programme for the prevention of, combating of, and care of victims of, trafficking in persons and the national fund for investment in prevention and the care of victims of trafficking in persons
rationale: Paraguay implemented a National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking 2020-2024 (extended to 2025-2026), designated the Ministry of the Interior as lead agency with a dedicated fund (2025), opened the Nasaindy Protection Centre and maintains a specialised prosecution unit; the Committee on Migrant Workers finds standards still unsatisfactory, the ECLJ reports declining case numbers since 2019, and CRC calls for a national anti-trafficking strategy and elimination of criadazgo.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1 para. 78; A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2 para. 26; A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3 para. 34
evidence_quotes:
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 78 — Paraguay: "The implementation of the National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking in Persons 2020-2024 consolidated the State's response ... It was therefore decided to extend the implementation of the Plan for the period 2025-2026"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 26 — Committee on Migrant Workers: "Paraguay had not yet achieved satisfactory standards in its fight against trafficking in persons and that children, especially those living on the street in the tri-border area, continued to be subjected to exploitation"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3), para. 34 — European Centre for Law and Justice: "the number of human trafficking cases that opened every year had decreased since 2019 due to corruption, impunity, lack of resources and inadequate victim support"

primary_theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery
action_summary: Combat trafficking in persons
grade_label: Partially implemented / steps taken, further action needed
text: Safeguard the land tenure systems for all, including indigenous people, and ensure they are protected from all forms of modern slavery, such as forced or compulsory labour and debt bondage
rationale: Paraguay implemented a National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking 2020-2024 (extended to 2025-2026), designated the Ministry of the Interior as lead agency with a dedicated fund (2025), opened the Nasaindy Protection Centre and maintains a specialised prosecution unit; the Committee on Migrant Workers finds standards still unsatisfactory, the ECLJ reports declining case numbers since 2019, and CRC calls for a national anti-trafficking strategy and elimination of criadazgo.
sources: A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1 para. 78; A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2 para. 26; A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/3 para. 34
evidence_quotes:
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/1), para. 78 — Paraguay: "The implementation of the National Plan to Prevent and Combat Trafficking in Persons 2020-2024 consolidated the State's response ... It was therefore decided to extend the implementation of the Plan for the period 2025-2026"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/52/PRY/2), para. 26 — Committee on Migrant Workers: "Paraguay had not yet achieved satisfactory standards in its fight against trafficking in persons and that children, especially those living on the street in the tri-border area, continued to be subjected to exploitation"
